 The Duchess has already appeared as a guest on the MasterChef Australia this year
 Tom Jeffreys
 Published 
 26 October 2026 10:05pm GMT
 The Duchess of Sussex will present the next season of the Australian version of Junior MasterChef.
 Meghan, who arrived back in Britain with the Duke of Sussex and their two children in August, may spend weeks filming the series in Melbourne next year.
 The Duchess will appear alongside Poh Ling Yeow, the MasterChef Australia judge, with the show set to air in 2027.
 She will be based in Australia during filming where the Duke, and their children – Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5 – may join her, but a final decision has not been made.
 The Duchess has already appeared as a guest on MasterChef Australia this year, taking a break from the couple’s four-day visit to the country in April to appear as a guest judge.
 The Duchess will appear alongside presenter Poh Ling Yeow
 Credit : Television Stills
 During the appearance, The Duke called her for a video chat while he was in Canberra meeting veterans.
 The news emerged after a turbulent week for the Duchess, during which it was revealed her father was being investigated by police in the Philippines on suspicion of possessing child abuse images.
 Thomas Markle Sr, who lives in the Philippines, is alleged to have kept “hundreds, if not thousands” of underage sexual images that the Duchess’s half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, says he discovered.
 Mr Markle Sr has strenuously denied the allegations against him.
 It later emerged that Meghan was warned about child sexual abuse allegations against her estranged father eight years ago in a letter written by Mr Markle Sr’s first wife.
 The letter was sent to the Metropolitan Police in 2019 but the force has admitted it did not act on it.
 ‘Upset and frustrated’
 The Met has since been criticised for inaction, with Jim Gamble , an international campaigner against child sexual abuse and former police chief, telling BBC Radio 4 that the contents of the letter should have been reported to the FBI .
 The force is assessing whether to refer itself to the police watchdog about its handling of the correspondence. It previously admitted it had not shared the allegations of child abuse contained in the letter with any overseas authorities.
 The Telegraph has revealed that Meghan is said to be “ upset and frustrated ” by the Met’s admission that it had not acted on the allegations.
 When the Duke and Duchess arrived back in the UK, it was reported that she was in advanced discussions to join the cast for the third season of The Gentlemen .
 It has since been claimed that the reports were a stunt to promote the television series. Sources close to the programme have denied the claims.
 Since the couple’s return, they have completed royal-style engagements in Nottingham, visiting several charities.
 However, sources close to them insisted that the Midlands visit was not a sign of things to come, with her priorities instead being motherhood, her lifestyle business and efforts to reboot her acting career.
